methodology: The study involved the preparation of concrete samples with different fiber contents (0.2% and 0.4%) as a substitution for sand weight, and lengths of fibers ranging from 10 to 30 mm. The specimens were exposed to an aqueous environment containing 3% sodium chloride for 365 days to study corrosion phenomena. Electrochemical techniques such as half-cell potential (HCP), electrochemical noise (EN), linear polarization resistance (LPR), and electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS) were applied.
research_objective: The objective of this work is to incorporate high-density recycled polyethylene fibers (HDPE) for possible use as reinforcement in concrete. The study aims to analyze physical and mechanical properties from recycled fibers, including density, absorption, stress resistance, workability, air content, porosity, compressive strength, flexural strength, and corrosion resistance.
